Ultraviolette Automotive Unveils New VX-100 Platform and X-47 Venom to Fuel Global Expansion

29 Oct 2026, 03:27 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Auto Desk · Source: www.business-standard.com

Image: Business Standard — Creative Commons

Key takeaways Expanding Global Reach and Manufacturing Footprint Electric motorcycle manufacturer Ultraviolette Automotive has announced a major strategic push into international markets, aiming for exports to account for 20 to 25 per cent of its total vehicle sales over the next t

Expanding Global Reach and Manufacturing Footprint

Electric motorcycle manufacturer Ultraviolette Automotive has announced a major strategic push into international markets, aiming for exports to account for 20 to 25 per cent of its total vehicle sales over the next two to three years. The Bengaluru-based company is targeting key regions including Europe, North America, and Latin America. As part of this expansion, Ultraviolette plans to establish a new 250,000-unit manufacturing facility in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, backed by an investment of approximately ₹800 crore. This new plant will feature multiple vehicle assembly lines and dedicated battery production lines, complementing the company's existing facility near Bengaluru, which currently has an annual capacity of up to 50,000 units.

The VX-100 Platform and X-47 Venom Launch

The export strategy coincides with the introduction of the company's new 100V electric vehicle architecture, known as the VX-100 platform. Alongside this platform launch, Ultraviolette debuted the X-47 Venom, the next generation of its X-47 Crossover and the inaugural motorcycle built on the new architecture. Bookings for the X-47 Venom have opened, with an introductory price of ₹2.65 lakh established for the first 5,000 units before shifting to a regular starting price of ₹3 lakh. The model is scheduled to make its European debut at the EICMA motorcycle show in Milan on November 3, as the company initially focuses on approximately 20 European nations, including Germany, France, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom.

Performance Specifications and Charging Capabilities

Engineered for high-performance riding alongside everyday usability, the X-47 Venom delivers a peak power output of 30 kW (40 hp) and 550 Nm of torque at the wheel. It achieves a top speed of 155 kmph and accelerates from 0 to 100 kmph in 5.9 seconds. With an Indian Driving Cycle (IDC) range of 343 km and a kerb weight of 180 kg—making it up to 20 kg lighter than its predecessor—the motorcycle integrates advanced features such as push-button cruise control and UV Hypersense radar intelligence. Furthermore, the model establishes a new benchmark in electric two-wheeler charging by supporting 12 kW DC fast charging.

Future Product Pipeline and Production Targets

Ultraviolette is preparing to roll out four products on the VX-100 platform over the coming year, which will include the anticipated Shockwave and Tesseract models alongside a mix of other motorcycles and scooters. Company leadership projects that monthly demand could surpass 10,000 vehicles by the end of the next financial year, scaling up to approximately 20,000 vehicles per month—split evenly between 10,000 scooters and 10,000 motorcycles—within a two-year timeframe following the new product rollouts.

Practical Implications and Reader Verification

What is Confirmed

  • Ultraviolette is investing ₹800 crore in a new manufacturing plant in Hosur, Tamil Nadu, targeting a 250,000-unit capacity.
  • The company launched the VX-100 platform and the X-47 Venom motorcycle, with an introductory price of ₹2.65 lakh for the first 5,000 units.
  • The X-47 Venom features a 343 km IDC range, 30 kW peak power, 12 kW DC fast-charging support, and a top speed of 155 kmph.
  • International expansion targets Europe, North America, and Latin America, with an initial focus on 20 European countries and an upcoming showcase at EICMA in Milan.

What Remains Unknown

  • Exact deployment timelines for North American and Latin American markets.
  • Finalized launch dates for the remaining three products on the VX-100 platform, including the Shockwave and Tesseract.
